title: Money Mule Networks
summary: How mule accounts are recruited, controlled and used to layer fraud proceeds, how to distinguish witting from unwitting mules, and how to dismantle the networks behind them.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How mule accounts are recruited, controlled and used to layer fraud proceeds, how to distinguish witting from unwitting mules, and how to dismantle the networks behind them.
Learning Objectives: Explain how mule networks are recruited and controlled
Identify indicators of mule accounts in financial data
Choose proportionate responses for different types of mule
Syllabus: Indicators of mule activity in account and payment data
Intended Audience: Fraud, economic crime and cybercrime investigators
FIU analysts handling fraud-related reports and urgent requests
Victim liaison, prevention and disruption officers working with the financial sector
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of fraud, cybercrime or financial crime investigation is helpful. No technical background in cyber security or crypto-assets is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2023), Illicit Financial Flows from Cyber-Enabled Fraud
FATF (2022), Partnering in the Fight Against Financial Crime: Data Protection, Technology and Private Sector Information Sharing
FATF (2021), Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers
